title: World Wide Web proposed and released
before: Internet services existed (FTP, email, etc.), but linking multimedia documents across servers lacked a simple universal hypertext system for the general public.
problem: CERN and the research world needed easier information sharing across different computers.
change: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the Web at CERN (1989) and the first website/HTTP/HTML stack emerged soon after; CERN documents a short history of these steps.
whyItMattered: URL + HTTP + HTML made distributed hypertext practical for everyone, not only networking specialists.
enabled: Browsers, web applications, e-commerce, and web-mediated software distribution.
concreteExample: Opening a documentation site in a browser uses the same core Web architecture ideas.
caveat: The Internet and the Web are not the same; the Web is an application layer built on internet protocols.
